Few professions shape daily life as visibly as civil engineering, and that is what first drew me to it. Growing up fascinated by how bridges, roads, and skylines shape the way people live and work, I pursued a Master’s degree at a university ranked in the global top 500, where I developed a strong interest in turning technical requirements into clear, buildable plans that balance safety, efficiency, and cost. Over time, that interest became more focused through practical work, including 4 completed projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my commitment to creating infrastructure that serves people well over time. One of my favourite memories was taking my family to a bridge project I helped build, hearing a younger relative proudly tell strangers, “They build these beautiful structures to look easy, but they also help people move safely across them.” That moment captured exactly why this field matters to me.

My academic training gave me a structured way of approaching complex technical work, and I have also learned how to carry work through over time. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas I have worked on before, and I value those exchanges because they keep engineering collaborative and useful.

I have also shown my commitment by staying with a lengthy stretch of work through several setbacks, adding extra hours when deadlines demanded it so that the work could still be completed properly. Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of technical grounding, project experience, and practical judgement to a Civil Engineer role where I can contribute to infrastructure that is resilient, safe, and genuinely useful to the communities it serves.

Alongside this, I have completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, and I am keen to bring that same care, accuracy, and sense of finish to a Carpenter role where I can contribute to spaces people rely on every day.
